title: Been working on my own idea of an idle/incremental MMO
author: CertainBlue
selftext:
It's funny because I've seen lots of people try to take their stab at making their own MMO. So here's my own attempt, which I'd say is not very ambitious: I wanted to make the kind of game that sits on your second monitor, where your character farms by itself and you can come back, craft the gear you need and fight a boss to progress. And my idea was to try to figure out my own niche, rather than just copying something that already exists, but this has been really tricky because I've been faced with lots of design problems without an easy solution. This isn't just another x or y game clone, this tries to be it's own original concept.  
  
Everything is completely made with AI, the code, the graphics, the music and SFX, even this trailer.   
It's still a work in progress, there's a whole bunch of rough edges, namely progression and gearing don't feel very good right now, there's only 4 tiers of progress of which there are 4 planned, possibly group content and dynamic events, etc...  
  
I'm just posting it to see if anyone resonates with it, it's a shot in the dark since there's so many of these these days.  
  
You can play it for free without registering here:   
[https://mmo-idle.up.railway.app/](https://mmo-idle.up.railway.app/)

comments.author: wildbling
comments.body:
wow this looks similar the the single player idle RPG I've been working on for the past month and half, I am using grok build to develop mine, I have crafting, classes, pets and AI companions, with a loot system similar to diablo2.  
You seem to have solved the tile logic but I can't seem to get the tile logic down like yours, what I mean is where the tiles will seamlessly angle around the corners to connect to each other down, how did you prompt it to work like that?   
I've included a screen of my current game, but as you can see my tiles are just squares and I can't get them to blend in and not look like they seamlessly fit or blend in. 

https://preview.redd.it/2f4quwrgthth1.jpeg?width=3826&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=b40289f5029403604d7f5cab4ef860c69367b3df

replies.author: CertainBlue
replies.body:
I'm using pixel labs to generate tilesets, it generates wang tiles that have variations for the corners, on top of that I have props that I add later. This approach is rather simple, you just need to find some generator that will generate the tileset for you and then wiring it up isn't hard. In my case I have a few different layout variations that I use for. Just google or ask your agents for wang tiles and it should be easy.

https://preview.redd.it/yulhqffcvhth1.png?width=256&format=png&auto=webp&s=9e35306858d5fc060b0a43988f8b3225434b38b3

replies.author: wildbling
replies.body:
So that's what they are called. Believe me, I 've prompted numerous times and trials for a seamless tileset but they never worked out. So ultimately I just gave up.   
I'll definitely give your suggestion a try. Thanks!
